text:
[LSER.7.6.1] Every series carries state per identity. That
identity is **declared, never inferred from a slot's name or
from an absence**: it is named explicitly with `by: <slot>` in
the block-options on the declaration, or follows the schema's
declared identity when `by:` is omitted:

- on a **`logical`** schema whose key is exactly one slot, an
  omitted `by:` groups by that slot ([LFAC.1.7]). A schema whose
  key is ∅ (every slot `mutable`) has no declared identity to
  follow, and the compiler must reject the declaration with
  `DS_VALIDATE_SERIES_NO_IDENTITY_SLOT` ([LSER.10.13]).
  `by: none` ([LSER.7.6.2]) is the explicit way to ask for a
  single global allocation.
- on a **`logical`** schema whose key is several slots, there is
  no default either: a composite key is not an identity a series
  can follow ([LSER.10.13] binds one slot), and the compiler must
  reject an omitted `by:` with the same code. The author names the
  one slot to group by, or `by: none`.
- on a schema of any other lifecycle (**`ttl`**, **`explicit`**,
  **`activation`**), which carries no identity markers
  ([LFAC.1.7.6]), there is no default: the declaration must
  name `by: <slot>` (or `by: none`) explicitly, and the compiler
  must reject an omitted `by:` with the same code.

The compiler errors on any `by:` naming a slot the schema does not
have. `entity_id` is an ordinary slot name with no
series-grouping privilege.

**One slot, and a composite key does not widen it.** A series row
is keyed on one identity value; grouping by a tuple would put
tuple construction and comparison on the absorb path of every
series, for a schema shape an author can express instead by
carrying the composite value in a slot of its own. Taking the
first `key` slot of a composite instead would silently merge entities
that differ only in the slots it drops, and that is the reading this
clause refuses.
